title: Music Theory: Summary and Reference
intro: The whole Music Theory topic on one page, for looking things up while you play. No sound examples here: each section links back to the page that explains it.

items: Note names A–G repeat every octave; middle C is C4; A4 = 440 Hz. An octave doubles the frequency.
12 semitones per octave. White-key semitones: E–F and B–C. Every other pair of neighbouring white keys is a whole tone (2 semitones).
♯ raises a semitone, ♭ lowers a semitone, ♮ cancels. Enharmonic: same key, two names (F♯ = G♭).
Treble clef lines E G B D F, spaces F A C E. Bass clef lines G B D F A, spaces A C E G.
Cents: 100 per equal-tempered semitone, 1200 per octave. Sound and Pitch (#/arts/music-theory/sound-and-pitch), Notation (#/arts/music-theory/sound-and-pitch/notation).
Whole = 2 halves = 4 quarters = 8 eighths = 16 sixteenths. A dot adds half the value; a tie joins two notes.
Simple meters divide the beat in two (2/4, 3/4, 4/4); compound meters in three (6/8, 9/8, 12/8).
Triplet: three notes in the time of two. Swing: pairs of eighths played long–short.
Rhythm and Meter (#/arts/music-theory/rhythm).

Inversion: numbers add to 9; major <-> minor, aug <-> dim, perfect stays perfect.

items: Major scale: W W H W W W H (C D E F G A B C).
Natural minor: W H W W H W W (A B C D E F G A). Harmonic minor raises the 7th; melodic minor raises the 6th and 7th going up.
Scale degrees: 1 tonic, 2 supertonic, 3 mediant, 4 subdominant, 5 dominant, 6 submediant, 7 leading tone.
Relative keys share a key signature (C major / A minor); parallel keys share a tonic (C major / C minor).
Order of sharps F C G D A E B; flats B E A D G C F. Sharp keys: tonic is a semitone above the last sharp. Flat keys: tonic is the second-to-last flat.
Modes (brightest to darkest): Lydian (♯4), Ionian, Mixolydian (♭7), Dorian (♭3 ♭7), Aeolian (♭3 ♭6 ♭7), Phrygian (adds ♭2), Locrian (adds ♭5).
Pentatonic: major 1 2 3 5 6; minor 1 ♭3 4 5 ♭7; blues adds ♭5.
Scales and Keys (#/arts/music-theory/scales-and-keys), Circle of Fifths (#/arts/music-theory/scales-and-keys/circle-of-fifths), Modes (#/arts/music-theory/scales-and-keys/modes).

items: Root: the note a chord is built on and named after; stack the notes in thirds and the bottom one is the root (Roots (#/arts/music-theory/chords/roots)).
Triads: major (M3 + m3), minor (m3 + M3), diminished (m3 + m3), augmented (M3 + M3).
Sevenths: maj7 (C E G B), 7 (C E G B♭), m7 (C E♭ G B♭), ø7 / m7♭5 (C E♭ G♭ B♭), °7 (C E♭ G♭ B𝄫).
Chords of a major key: I ii iii IV V vi vii°; with sevenths Imaj7 ii7 iii7 IVmaj7 V7 vi7 viiø7. Minor key (with the raised 7th in V and vii°): i ii° III iv V VI vii°.

Inversions: root position (root in the bass), first inversion (3rd in the bass, figure 6), second inversion (5th in the bass, 6/4); sevenths 7, 6/5, 4/3, 4/2. Slash chords: C/E = C with E in the bass.
Extensions: 9 = 2, 11 = 4, 13 = 6, an octave up. sus4 replaces the 3rd with the 4th; add9 adds the 9th without a 7th.
Chords (#/arts/music-theory/chords), Inversions (#/arts/music-theory/chords/inversions), Extended and Altered Chords (#/arts/music-theory/chords/extended-and-altered).
Functions: tonic (I, vi), predominant (IV, ii), dominant (V, vii°). Phrases move T → PD → D → T.
Strongest root motion: down a fifth (V → I, ii → V).
Cadences: authentic V–I (perfect: root positions, tonic on top), half (ends on V), plagal IV–I, deceptive V–vi.
Voice leading: keep common tones, move other voices by step, resolve the leading tone up and chord sevenths down, avoid parallel fifths and octaves.
Secondary dominants: V of any major or minor chord (in C: D7 → G, A7 → Dm, E7 → Am).
Modulation: a pivot chord common to both keys, then a cadence in the new key.
Borrowed chords (from the parallel minor): iv, ♭VI, ♭VII. Neapolitan: ♭II6. Augmented sixths: Italian, French, German, expanding to V.
Harmony (#/arts/music-theory/harmony), Cadences (#/arts/music-theory/harmony/cadences), Voice Leading (#/arts/music-theory/harmony/voice-leading).
First species: consonances only; begin and end on perfect consonances; no parallel fifths or octaves; mostly steps; leaps recovered by a step back.
Phrase: a musical thought ending in a cadence. Period: antecedent (weak cadence) + consequent (strong cadence). Sentence: 2 + 2 + 4 bars.
Forms: binary AB, ternary ABA, rondo ABACA, sonata (exposition, development, recapitulation), 12-bar blues, 32-bar AABA, verse–chorus.
Counterpoint (#/arts/music-theory/counterpoint), Form (#/arts/music-theory/form).
ii–V–I (Dm7–G7–Cmaj7); guide tones are the 3rds and 7ths. Tritone substitution: D♭7 for G7.
Just intervals: octave 2/1, fifth 3/2, fourth 4/3, major third 5/4, minor third 6/5. Equal temperament: every semitone $2^{1/12}$; its major third is 13.7 cents wider than 5/4.
Pythagorean comma ≈ 23.46 cents (12 fifths vs 7 octaves); syntonic comma 81/80 ≈ 21.5 cents.
Pitch classes 0–11 (C = 0); sets named by prime form; twelve-tone rows in P, I, R and RI forms.
Jazz Harmony (#/arts/music-theory/jazz-harmony), Tuning (#/arts/music-theory/tuning), Post-Tonal Theory (#/arts/music-theory/post-tonal).
